dailyTopNewsBrief.headline: Jesse Minter Takes Accountability as Ravens Drop Sixth Straight in Carolina
dailyTopNewsBrief.summary: Baltimore dropped to 4-7 following a 35-33 setback to the Carolina Panthers, extending the NFL's longest active losing streak to six games and reducing their playoff probability to 5.6% ahead of Week 12.
bullets: Head Coach Jesse Minter publicly claimed full responsibility after Baltimore surrendered 35 points to Carolina, though the unit continues to rank #26 in scoring defense (26.7 PPG allowed) and #25 in turnover differential (-4) [Jesse Minter](https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/50567139/jesse-minter-take-responsibility-latest-ravens-loss).

Ravens defensive leaders Roquan Smith and Kyle Hamilton pushed back against Minter taking sole blame, acknowledging recurring communication lapses and trust issues during Bryce Young's late game-winning drive [baltimoreravens.com Official](https://www.baltimoreravens.com/news/ravens-defensive-leaders-shoulder-loss-panthers-jesse-minter-kyle-hamilton-roquan-smith).

Offensively, wide receiver Zay Flowers caught eight passes for 97 yards, but self-inflicted mistakes and late-game stalls hampered quarterback Jacoby Brissett in complementary execution [baltimoreravens.com Video](https://www.baltimoreravens.com/video/zay-flowers-panthers-ravens-week-11-press-conferences).

Looking ahead to Week 12 at Houston (4-6), Baltimore's top-nine rushing attack (125.6 YPG) must contend with a Texans defense holding the NFL's #2 sack rate (9.5%), while Baltimore operates with $6.63M in 2026 cap space [NFL Nation](https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/50563342/week-11-sunday-games-takeaways-questions-2026).
